prompt:
Act as the fresh-agent novelty reviewer required by the novelty-check skill. Date: 2026-08-10. Research context: OLMoE experiments show execution shape changes BF16 expert outputs and can propagate into downstream ordered top-k route changes and at least one stable token flip. A fresh 240-cell pre-action selectability gate failed (oracle +57, matched shuffle -4, static/online -7), so do not revive pre-action row selectors. Simple expert-output BF16 bitmask/dither canonicalization also failed: at M=2, only 12/160 rows raw-equal; dropping all 7 mantissa bits makes 104/160 equal at median relative L2 distortion 31.2%. Review novelty of exactly these three candidates, brutally and independently:

1) RouteSnap / RouterCanon: define a versioned deterministic lattice for MoE router logits at inference. Expert indices are chosen from snapped logits with fixed expert-ID tie-breaking; mixing weights may remain from raw logits. Apply at every router to make the discrete control plane less sensitive to execution-shape-induced hidden drift, without making all kernels batch-invariant. Frozen per-layer snap steps and a semantic budget/escape path. Main claim: low-cost control-plane canonicalization can recover cross-shape route consistency with far lower overhead than whole-model batch-invariant kernels.

2) TenantShapeFence: treat execution-shape dependence as a cross-request integrity channel in multi-tenant MoE serving even when there is no expert-capacity overflow or token dropping. Carry a security-domain/tenant tag through expert dispatch and batch grouped expert rows by (expert, domain), so untrusted tenants cannot change another domain's expert GEMM M/kernel regime; same-domain rows may still batch. Certified batch-invariant kernels may opt into safe cross-domain merging. Main claim: numerical noninterference domains prevent co-batch-induced victim route/token changes at much lower cost than singleton/full batch-invariant inference.

3) IntervalTopK / RouteCert: obtain an expert-output or cumulative hidden error envelope, propagate it through router weights to logit intervals, certify top-k if kth lower bound exceeds (k+1)th upper, and escalate only uncertified tokens. Main claim: middle-layer proof rather than heuristic margin prediction.

Known closest work that MUST be considered:
- Thinking Machines 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference'; vLLM and SGLang batch-invariant inference; DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end batch-invariant/deterministic kernels; TBIK arXiv:2511.17826.
- LLM-42 arXiv:2601.17768 verified replay; MarginGate arXiv:2605.30218 output-margin verification.
- NeurIPS 2025 LayerCast arXiv:2506.09501.
- Buffer Overflow in Mixture of Experts arXiv:2402.05526: malicious co-batches change victims via capacity-limited, cross-batch-dependent routing; default no-capacity Mixtral was not vulnerable.
- StableMoE arXiv:2204.08396 (training-time fluctuation/distilled frozen router).
- DREAM-MoE (2026 OpenReview Wyhqwjl51A), EAQuant, EAC-MoE, ExpertQuant, VSRAQ arXiv:2606.05688: preserve routing under model quantization.
- Recent OpenReview TMLR submission bPsPPI65hf gives top-k gap condition under router quantization.

Search current primary literature yourself, especially last 6 months, and return: core claims, closest papers table, novelty score /10 per candidate, PROCEED/CAUTION/ABANDON, exact honest differentiator, fatal collision risk, and which one is most likely to support a CCF-C/B systems paper IF its first oracle pilot succeeds.
